To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of the k- turbulence model allows the accurate prediction of the flutter derivatives of the bridge cross section, with a computational effort that is affordable.
the use of a k-ω turbulence closure model is a good choice for FSI applications.
the k- turbulence model is a reliable tool to predict the unsteady aerodynamics on bluff bodies, including bridges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of the k- turbulence model in FSI problems.
the assessment of the k-turbulence model performance in FSI applications.
the application of CFD techniques to the assessment of the aerodynamic forces induced by the wind on a long span bridge, in order to predict its dynamic response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the k-ω turbulence model is able to accurately reproduce the steady and transient aerodynamic loads acting on a bridge section.
the use of k- turbulence model is a reliable and accurate approach for predicting aerodynamic forces and flutter derivatives of long span bridges.
the use of the k-turbulence model, in the context of a specific simulation methodology, allows to accurately reproduce the aerodynamic forces on a Great Belt bridge cross section.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the k-turbulence model is able to reproduce the experimental evidence for both the test cases and for the Great Belt bridge.
the k-turbulence model is able to predict the steady and unsteadiness aerodynamic forces induced by the wind on the Great Belt East Bridge with good accuracy.
the k- turbulence models are a suitable approach for FSI problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the k-turbulence model can be used for FSI applications in which the Reynolds number is in the range of 105-106 and in the absence of separation.
